title: Fix context-gather backtick crash
root_cause: spawn-worker.sh line 92 uses execSync (shell-invoking) to run opencode. The prompt is injected via JS template literal + JSON.stringify(). JSON.stringify does NOT escape backticks — they're valid JSON. When the prompt contains JS template literals from gathered source files, the backticks land inside a bash double-quoted string where bash interprets them as command substitution. Unbalanced backticks (from truncated context) cause 'Syntax error: end of file unexpected' and exit 2.
heredoc_is_safe: The heredoc at line 85 uses a single-quoted delimiter (<< 'NODESCRIPT'), so bash writes the JS content literally. Backticks in the heredoc body are never interpreted. The bug is NOT in the heredoc — it's in the generated JS's use of execSync.

fix.strategy: Replace execSync with execFileSync in the generated Node.js runner to bypass shell interpretation entirely

changes.description: Replace execSync (shell) with execFileSync (no shell). Build args array instead of template literal string. This eliminates all shell metacharacter issues — backticks, $(), quotes, pipes, etc.

fix.note: execFileSync passes args as an array directly to the process, never through a shell. Backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes — all literal. No sanitization needed.

why_not_sanitize_context_output: Stripping backticks from context-gather.sh would lose code fidelity — developers need to see actual source. Escaping (doubling backslashes) is fragile and platform-dependent. The root cause is shell invocation in the runner, not the data content.
why_not_remove_heredoc: The heredoc is already safe (single-quoted delimiter). Replacing it with printf or base64 encoding adds complexity for no benefit.

secondary_fix.description: Remove the --no-context workaround documentation as it becomes unnecessary after the primary fix.

verification: Create a test prompt file containing JS template literals: const x = `hello ${name}`;
Run: scripts/spawn-worker.sh sprinter crafter /tmp/test-project /tmp/test-prompt.txt (with context — should NOT crash)
Verify worker status hits /api/agent-status with 'working' before opencode and 'idle' after
